opportunities.title: AXA New Gen 2026 Postdoctoral Fellowship - Responsible Nature-Based Solutions for a Resilient, Sustainable and Inclusive Future
opportunities.funder: AXA Foundation for Human Progress (formerly AXA Research Fund)
opportunities.program: AXA New Gen (Science pillar) - 2026 call on Responsible Nature-Based Solutions
opportunities.deadline_text: Step 1: Expression of Interest: October 20 - November 12, 2026 (4 PM CET). Institutions not yet registered in the platform must register by November 3, 2026 (4 PM CET) to submit EOI. Step 2: Full application (for shortlisted candidates only): November 24 - December 17, 2026 (4 PM CET)
opportunities.funding_text: The AXA New Gen is awarded for a maximum amount of 140,000EUR in total, to be spent over two years. ... The budget will help cover: Annual salary of the researcher (based on institution internal policy); Equipment/resources (databases, survey costs, consumables, etc.); Academic activities (conferences, workshops, fieldwork, etc.); Outreach activities (beyond academic audiences). ... Overhead costs are NOT eligible.
opportunities.duration: 2 years ('An AXA New Gen Fellowship is awarded for a period of 2 years.'); projects expected to start before June 2028
opportunities.eligible_applicants: Host institution applies on behalf of ONE early-career candidate per institution. Hosts: academic institutions (registered in WHED) and public research organizations. Candidate: PhD defended within the last 5 years before 10 Oct 2026 (+6 months per child), no permanent (tenured/tenure-track) position, full-time on the project.
opportunities.cgiar_eligibility_notes: Hosts must be universities or public research organizations; 'Associations, foundations, governmental bodies, hospitals, independent research centers, museums, and NGOs are not eligible for AXA funding.' The Alliance/CIAT is an international (treaty-based) research organization - not clearly a 'public research organization' and possibly read as an 'independent research center'. Must be confirmed with science.foundation@axa.com before 3 Nov 2026 registration deadline. Safer route: the candidate is hosted by a partner university (e.g., a Colombian or European university) with the Alliance as a societal/non-academic partner. Also note the fellowship is for the candidate's own salary - the candidate must meet PhD+5 and no permanent position rules.
opportunities.lead_applicant_requirements: Institution's Operational Contact submits EOI in English: candidate details (date of birth, PhD defense date), short CV (max 2 pages), research project description (max 3,000 characters). Researcher must hold PhD for no more than 5 years and not hold a permanent position.
opportunities.consortium_details: Project must include at least one transdisciplinary aspect: (i) collaboration across disciplines (social sciences/humanities/economics AND natural/environmental sciences/engineering/technology) and (ii) societal partners (public authorities, communities, civil society organizations, practitioners). Private for-profit companies are not eligible as project partners.
opportunities.cofunding_details: 'Host institutions will be expected to participate in the AXA New Gen's general funding with studentships, PhD support, and material resources ... There is no minimum requirement for the institution's contribution. However, a larger contribution makes the proposal more attractive.'
opportunities.eligible_activities: Postdoctoral research on nature-based solutions: disaster risk reduction and adaptation; food and water security under climate stress ('NbS for sustainable agriculture, forest and landscape restoration, and water resources management'); urban green infrastructure; health/cultural dimensions; economic models and financing of NbS; governance and social justice.
opportunities.required_documents: EOI: candidate details, 2-page CV, 3,000-character project description. Full application (shortlisted): detailed research program, CV and publication list, letters of support (supervisor at host institution and an academic and/or non-academic partner), budget incl. host contribution.
opportunities.application_procedure: Host institution registers on https://institution.axa-research.org (by 3 Nov 2026), Operational Contact submits EOI by 12 Nov 2026 16:00 CET; shortlisted full application 24 Nov - 17 Dec 2026; rebuttal 30 Mar - 5 Apr 2027; results June 2027.
opportunities.scientific_alignment_rationale: NbS for agriculture/landscape restoration and food security under climate stress fits Multifunctional Landscapes; RS/EO and crop modelling can quantify NbS trade-offs, but a social-science component is mandatory.
opportunities.strategic_relevance_rationale: Directly matches Alliance Multifunctional Landscapes/climate action agenda; global call; prestigious early-career salary support.
opportunities.technical_feasibility_rationale: Feasible technically; binding constraints are the candidate profile (PhD+5, non-permanent), the host-institution eligibility question and the very short EOI window.
opportunities.recommendation: Pursue only if (a) the researcher (or a junior Alliance postdoc) defended the PhD after ~Oct 2021 and has no permanent post, and (b) AXA confirms the Alliance can host, or a partner university agrees to host. Only one candidate per institution - coordinate early.
opportunities.potential_partners: Colombian universities (e.g., Universidad Nacional de Colombia, Universidad del Valle, Universidad de los Andes) as host; local governments/community organizations as societal partners.
opportunities.next_action: Email science.foundation@axa.com this week asking whether the Alliance of Bioversity International and CIAT (international research organization) qualifies as a host; in parallel identify a university host and check its Operational Contact registration before 3 Nov 2026.

opportunities.title: Branco Weiss Fellowship - Society in Science 2027 (5-year postdoctoral fellowship, up to CHF 600,000)
opportunities.funder: The Branco Weiss Fellowship - Society in Science (private endowment, administered by ETH Zurich)
opportunities.deadline_text: January 15, 2027, 5 p.m. CET: final deadline for applications via the online form.
opportunities.funding_text: Fellows are awarded a fellowship amounting to a maximum of CHF 600,000 for a maximum of five years to carry out their research project. ... The host institution is allowed to retain a management fee not exceeding 10% of the fellowship.
opportunities.duration: Up to 5 years (2.5-year pioneer phase + 2.5-year exploitation phase after review/site visit); start between 1 Oct and 1 Jan following selection (Oct-Dec 2027).
opportunities.eligible_applicants: Individual postdocs of any nationality and discipline who obtained their PhD a maximum of five years before the submission deadline (i.e., on/after ~15 Jan 2022); professors/lecturers (incl. tenure-track) and scientists with permanent employment are not eligible. Requires invitation letter from a mentor at the host institution.
opportunities.eligible_countries: Any nationality; any academic host institution worldwide.
opportunities.cgiar_eligibility_notes: Applicant is an individual; the Alliance would act as host institution. Guidelines say 'any academic host institution worldwide' - whether a CGIAR center counts as 'academic' is not stated (to confirm with brancoweissfellowship@ethz.ch). Two personal blockers to check: PhD date must be within 5 years of 15 Jan 2027, and 'Scientists with a permanent employment are not eligible'. Alternative: a university host with Alliance as field partner.
opportunities.lead_applicant_requirements: PhD within 5 years before deadline; not a professor/lecturer; no permanent employment; mentor invitation letter guaranteeing independence and infrastructure; project must depart from mainstream research and engage with societal issues.
opportunities.geographic_restrictions: None ('in the best possible locations, anywhere in the world'); annual symposium in Zurich mandatory.
opportunities.consortium_details: Individual fellowship; one or more host institutions possible (one main host).
opportunities.cofunding_details: Host may partially fund the fellow's employment; not required.
opportunities.eligible_activities: Any scientific field; unconventional, beyond-mainstream research with a society dimension. Funds may cover fellow's salary, doctoral students' salaries, equipment, consumables, travel, technical services.
opportunities.required_documents: Project description (max 5 pages), lay abstract, CV with publications (max 4 pages), motivation letter on why the research differs from the mainstream (1 page), three publications, 5 reviewer suggestions, PhD certificate, invitation letter from mentor.
opportunities.application_procedure: Online form at brancoweissfellowship.org by 15 Jan 2027 17:00 CET; shortlisting and external peer review (May 2027 notifications); video interviews June 2027; start Oct-Dec 2027.
opportunities.scientific_alignment_rationale: Open to all fields, so RS/AI/crop-modelling projects qualify, but the scheme explicitly rewards research 'beyond the mainstream' - a standard digital-agriculture project would be screened out.
opportunities.strategic_relevance_rationale: Rare 5-year, salary-covering, globally portable fellowship (CHF 600k) - excellent for building an independent research line hosted at/with the Alliance.
opportunities.technical_feasibility_rationale: Requires an unusual, high-risk idea and strong individual track record; personal eligibility (PhD date, permanent contract) unknown.
opportunities.recommendation: Strongly consider if the researcher's PhD was awarded on/after ~15 Jan 2022 and their CIAT contract is not permanent; frame a non-mainstream idea (e.g., foundation models + process-based crop models for climate-intervention scenarios). Confirm host eligibility of the Alliance.
opportunities.potential_partners: University of Tokyo or ETH Zurich groups as co-host/mentor; Alliance as main or field host.
opportunities.next_action: Check PhD date and contract type; email brancoweissfellowship@ethz.ch whether a CGIAR center is an acceptable 'academic host institution'; secure a mentor invitation letter by December 2026.

evidence.deadline_quote: January 15, 2027, 5 p.m. CET: final deadline for applications via the online form.
evidence.eligibility_quote: The Fellowship is open to researchers from all disciplines and to citizens of all nationalities. ... opportunities.title: Wellcome Discovery Awards (team awards up to 8 years; rolling) - location rules change 29 Oct 2026
opportunities.deadline_text: There are no deadlines for applications to this scheme. Applications can be submitted at any time. (Shortlisting twice a year; interviews twice a year.) Location rule change: 'From 29 October 2026, we will only accept applications from lead applicants based at eligible administering organisations in the UK and low- and middle-income countries in Africa, South Asia and South-East Asia. Any applications submitted to Wellcome on or before 28 October 2026 will be assessed under the current location eligibility requirements.'
opportunities.funding_text: The average size of a Discovery Award is GBP 3.5 million. Applications above GBP 5 million will be subject to additional scrutiny.
opportunities.duration: Awards can be up to 8 years, but may be less for some disciplines (average 7 years; supported awards from 3 to 8 years).
opportunities.eligible_applicants: Established researchers with international standing leading teams (usually 2-8 applicants), at eligible not-for-profit administering organisations (higher education institutions, research institutes, healthcare organisations). Coapplicants may be based anywhere except mainland China.
opportunities.eligible_countries: Until 28 Oct 2026: UK, Republic of Ireland, LMICs (excl. India and mainland China). From 29 Oct 2026: lead applicant in UK or LMICs in Africa, South Asia and South-East Asia only (Latin America excluded for lead).
opportunities.cgiar_eligibility_notes: From 29 Oct 2026 a Colombia-based (CIAT HQ) lead is NOT eligible. A lead based at an Alliance office in an eligible African or Asian LMIC (e.g., Kenya, Viet Nam) could apply if that office qualifies as a not-for-profit research institute administering organisation - to confirm with Wellcome. LAC-based Alliance staff can join as coapplicants (anywhere except mainland China). Remit is a hard constraint: research must have 'the potential to improve human life, health, and wellbeing' (e.g., climate-nutrition-health pathways), not agriculture per se.
opportunities.lead_applicant_requirements: Established researcher with international standing; lead applicant salary only if based in an LMIC with a permanent/long-term contract and reliant on external grant funding.
opportunities.geographic_restrictions: Primary location of the research, including leadership, must be in the UK, Ireland and/or an LMIC (rules tightening on 29 Oct 2026 as above).
opportunities.consortium_details: Teams usually 2-8 applicants including the lead; collaborators allowed without eligibility restriction.
opportunities.eligible_activities: Bold, creative discovery research in any discipline relevant to human life, health and wellbeing (incl. climate-health links).
opportunities.required_documents: Not specified on scheme summary; application via Wellcome Funding Platform.
opportunities.application_procedure: Submit via Wellcome Funding Platform at any time; shortlisting committee, interview, decision.
opportunities.scientific_alignment_rationale: Methods (EO, AI, crop modelling) are relevant only if the question is a human-health one (e.g., climate shocks -> crop nutrition/food security -> health outcomes).
opportunities.strategic_relevance_rationale: One of very few philanthropic schemes paying full research-staff salaries for up to 8 years; Alliance Africa/Asia hubs are in eligible regions.
opportunities.technical_feasibility_rationale: Needs an established health-research co-lead and an Africa/Asia-based lead; large, competitive scheme.
opportunities.recommendation: Worth pursuing only as a team with a health/nutrition co-lead and an Alliance Africa/Asia-based lead (e.g., climate-driven crop yield and nutrient shocks and child nutrition). Not suitable for a Colombia-based lead after 28 Oct 2026.
opportunities.potential_partners: KEMRI-Wellcome Trust (Kenya), MLW (Malawi), OUCRU (Viet Nam), LSHTM Centre on Climate Change and Planetary Health, IFPRI (nutrition).
opportunities.next_action: Discuss with Alliance Africa/Asia colleagues whether the Nairobi or Hanoi office can be a Wellcome administering organisation; identify a health co-lead.

opportunities.title: Wellcome Early-Career Awards and Career Development Awards (personal salary + team, 5-8 years; rolling)
opportunities.program: Discovery Research - Early-Career Awards / Career Development Awards
opportunities.deadline_text: There are no deadlines for applications to this scheme. Applications can be submitted at any time. (Shortlisting three times a year: February, June, September.) Location eligibility changes from 29 October 2026 (lead in UK or LMICs in Africa, South Asia and South-East Asia only).
opportunities.funding_text: Early-Career Award: 'Your salary and up to GBP 400,000 for research expenses.' Career Development Award: 'The annual expenditure for a Career Development Award is usually below GBP 250,000 excluding the applicant's salary.' (funding_amount_max refers to ECA research expenses; CDA has no stated total cap)
opportunities.duration: Early-Career Award: usually 5 years. Career Development Award: usually 8 years.
opportunities.eligible_applicants: ECA: early-career researchers with PhD (or equivalent) and up to 3 years postdoctoral experience. CDA: mid-career researchers already leading their own research. Hosted by eligible not-for-profit administering organisations.
opportunities.eligible_countries: Until 28 Oct 2026: UK, Ireland, LMICs (excl. India, mainland China). From 29 Oct 2026: lead in UK or LMICs in Africa, South Asia and South-East Asia only.
opportunities.cgiar_eligibility_notes: Colombia-based researchers are effectively ineligible from 29 Oct 2026 (applications on or before 28 Oct 2026 are judged under old rules - too short to be realistic). Possible only if the fellow is based at an Alliance office in an eligible African/Asian LMIC and that office qualifies as an administering organisation. LMIC-based applicants with permanent contracts can still request own salary. Remit must be human health-related.
opportunities.lead_applicant_requirements: ECA: up to 3 years postdoc experience at submission. CDA: mid-career, leading own research; permanent posts generally started within last 3 years.
opportunities.eligible_activities: Innovative research in any discipline with potential to improve human life, health and wellbeing.
opportunities.required_documents: Not specified on scheme summary; application via Wellcome Funding Platform.
opportunities.application_procedure: Rolling submission on Wellcome Funding Platform; shortlisting and interview rounds three times a year.
opportunities.scientific_alignment_rationale: Same remit constraint as Discovery Awards - needs a health outcome framing.
opportunities.strategic_relevance_rationale: Among the longest salary-funded fellowships available (5-8 years, plus up to 4 FTE staff for CDA).
opportunities.technical_feasibility_rationale: Requires relocation to/affiliation with an Alliance Africa/Asia office and a health-oriented research programme.
opportunities.recommendation: Relevant for Alliance staff based in Kenya or Viet Nam working on climate-food-health links; not for Colombia-based staff after 28 Oct 2026.
opportunities.next_action: Flag to Alliance Africa/Asia teams; confirm administering-organisation eligibility with Wellcome funding information team.
